content_md:
# Blygger Studio 0.11

  Blygger Studio, the reference client most blygs run on, has had its biggest change
  since it was split out of the spec repo. Three releases went out in three days.
  The core of it is the work of a new contributor, Kyle Mathews, who rebuilt the
  Studio in two pull requests.

  The Studio is now a React app. Compose, the editors, reading, subscriptions,
  hoppers, mentions and settings were all rebuilt. If you use it, it should look
  familiar: same layout, same themes, same features. What changed is underneath.
  Saving is safer: a failed save keeps what you typed, publishing waits for the save
  to finish, and leaving the editor saves first.

  The private API is now a documented contract. Every operation the Studio uses is
  described in an OpenAPI file and has a generated JavaScript SDK. So anyone
  building a tool for blyg authors, whether a desktop editor, a Drafts action or an
  agent, now has a real, published interface to build against. Several old routes
  changed. Tool authors should read the route table in the upgrade guide.

  My own additions in 0.11:

  - Images now travel between blygs. Until now, an image in a post showed up broken
    in other people's reading feeds, because its address only made sense on the blyg
    it came from. Studio now publishes full addresses, fixes up the ones it
    imports, and repairs what it had already imported.
  - Thread cards on the front page show the thread. You get the top of it as it
    looks on its own page, quotes and formatting included, not a flattened excerpt.
  - Images can go anywhere while you write. Type /image on a line by itself, or
    paste or drop an image, and it lands where your cursor is.

  None of this changes the protocol. Your blyg's public pages, feed and item files
  stay compatible with every other blyg, whatever software it runs.

  If you run your own blyg, most of you are on 0.8.x. Read Upgrading to 0.11
  (https://github.com/blygger/blygger-studio/blob/v0.11.0/docs/upgrading-to-0.11.md)
  before you upgrade. It covers both upgrade paths, one small database migration,
  the new build step, path-mounted blygs, how to check it worked, and how to roll
  back. Full details are in the changelog
  (https://github.com/blygger/blygger-studio/blob/v0.11.0/CHANGELOG.md).

  Thanks to Kyle for a contribution that came in with nearly a thousand tests and a
  three-minute demo video.
